full_judgment: 2. The case of the plaintiff was to the effect that he is an M.B.B.S (Cal.) D.T.M. (Bengal) and was appointed as Medical Officer in the Calcutta Medical College. After partition of India the plaintiff opted for Pakistan and was posted at Dhaka Medical College as Demonstrator of Pathology. Ultimately in February, 1950 the plaintiff was absorbed in East Pakistan Medical Service (Upper). While the plaintiff was serving as such, on 6th December, 1951 his service was terminated by the then Province of East Pakistan on the ground of his having over-stayed the leave granted to him without giving any show cause notice. The plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 34 of 1957 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka for declaration that the order of dismissal from service was illegal void, inoperative and that he was still a member of the then East Pakistan Medical Service (Upper). On 30.1.59 the suit was dismissed by the trial court. On appeal the learned District Judge. Dhaka by his judgment and decree dated 18.1.60 in Title Appeal No. 61 of 1959 set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit. A second appeal being Second Appeal No. 696 of 1960 was preferred by the Government against the said judgment and decree passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The Second Appeal was dismissed on 7.6.62. Thereafter a petition of special leave to appeal being C.P.S.L.A No. 49-D or 1962 was filed before the Supreme Court of Pakistan by the defendant No. 1. That was also dismissed on 21.11.1962. As such the plaintiff became entitled to reinstatement and the plaintiff made representation to the defendant for his reinstatement and also for payment of arrear salary. The defendant deferred any action in the said representation initially on the plea that they have filed a special leave petition before the Supreme Court of Pakistan. But after the dismissal of their petition the defendant intimated to the plaintiff by Memo No. S-1/1A-45/ 62/653 dated 30.7.1963 that the plaintiff was not entitled to either reinstatement or the arrears of salary. Thereafter the plaintiff filed a Writ Petition being Writ Petition No. 460 of 1963 in the High Court of East Pakistan under Article 98 of the then Constitution for enforcement of the decree but the High Court by its order dated 27.11.63 rejected the petition on the ground that there was nothing to be enforced. Thereafter the plaintiff field a petition against the said order of the High Court to the Supreme Court being Special leave to Appeal No. 1-D of 1964. The Supreme Court by its order dated 16.3.1964 dismissed the petition after observing that this is an unusual case in which the Government of East Pakistan is refusing to honour the decision of its own courts as it is expected to do. Now the plaintiff claims in this suit arrears of salary of Rs.1,00,950/- from November, 1951 to the date of the institution of the suit and by subsequent amendment further claimed arrears of salary from July, 1965 to August, 1969 totaling in all Rs. 1,24,350/-.
